mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% q/q in the last three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.05) during episodes where GDPC1 declines for two straight quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-mo moving average for six consecutive months
regime_hint: supply chain stress or manufacturing downturn
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% over two months signals a deflationary monetary regime, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) over three months signals robust household demand, which boosts consumption and investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both rise for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both PAYEMS and HOUST rise for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals labor market strength, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.05) during four consecutive months of above-trend payroll employment growth.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in real retail sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months, combined with stable inflation (CPIAUCSL change < 0.2% per month), signals improving consumer demand without inflationary pressure, which supports corporate margins and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo moving average for two months AND |CPIAUCSL change| < 0.2% per month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average for two months and inflation is stable.
